passages.text: Time flies, nights pass by, the stages of life leave us one by one. Seeing this peril in death, do good deeds that bring you joy.
passages.note: Time passing, mortality, using life well

passages.text: They don’t grieve for the past, nor do they pray for the future; they feed on whatever comes that day, that’s why their complexion’s so clear. Because they pray for the future, and grieve for the past, fools wither away, like a green reed mowed down.
passages.note: Regret about the past, anxiety about the future

passages.text: Children bring you sorrow. Cattle also bring you sorrow. For attachments are a man’s sorrow; without attachments there are no sorrows.
passages.note: Attachment as the root of sorrow and worry

passages.text: A mendicant should collect their thoughts as a tortoise draws its limbs into its shell. Independent, not disturbing others, quenched: they wouldn’t blame anyone.
passages.note: Gathering a scattered mind; not blaming others

passages.text: If you think that ‘I’m equal, special, or worse’, you’ll dispute about that.
passages.note: Comparing yourself to others breeds conflict

passages.text: Whoever wrongs a man who has done no wrong, a pure man who has not a blemish, the evil backfires on the fool, like fine dust thrown upwind.
passages.note: Being wronged unfairly; harm returns to the wrongdoer

passages.text: Tangled within, tangled without: these people are tangled in tangles. I ask you this, Gotama: who can untangle this tangle? A wise person grounded in ethics, developing the mind and wisdom, a keen and alert mendicant—they can untangle this tangle.
passages.note: Feeling tangled up inside and out; finding a way through

passages.text: You need not shield the mind from everything, nor has the mind gained self-control. The mind need only be shielded from where the bad things come.
passages.note: Guarding the mind wisely, not avoiding everything
